hook.line: Don Hernando loves to ask whether you remember the old Bogotá, and you will want to answer without tripping over a little word. Spanish has two ways to remember, and they treat the thing remembered differently.
hook.es: Me acuerdo perfectamente de esa tarde.

examples.es: Me acuerdo perfectamente de esa tarde.

examples.en: I remember his face very well.
Did you remember to pay the electricity bill? (to a friend)

examples.es: Me acordé de que era su cumpleaños.
examples.en: I remembered that it was her birthday.

examples.es: No me acuerdo de su nombre.

rule:
Two verbs, one meaning:

*recordar* takes the thing directly: *Recuerdo su cara.*
*acordarse* always comes with *me, te, se…* and then *de*: *Me acuerdo de su cara.*

After *de*, you can put a noun, an infinitive (*Te acordaste de pagar* = you remembered to pay) or a whole clause with *de que*.

English "remember" has no little *de*, so it is easy to drop. Never mix them: not *recuerdo de*, not *me acuerdo su cara*.
smallPrint: *Acordarse* is a pronominal verb: the *me/te/se* is part of it, not a separate object.

options: I remember his face very well.
I remind him of his face.
Did you remember to pay the electricity bill?
Did you remember paying the electricity bill?

readAndPick.es: Me acordé de que era su cumpleaños.
options: I remembered that it was her birthday.

readAndPick.es: No me acuerdo de su nombre.
Nunca me acuerdo de cerrar la puerta.
options: I never remember closing the door.
I never remember to close the door.
I remember that Rosa always sang.
I remember that Rosa always sings.

readAndPick.es: Me acuerdo de que Rosa siempre cantaba.
options: I remember Rosa always singing to me.
I remember that Rosa always sang.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Recuerdo* or *Me acuerdo* and type the whole sentence: *___ de esa tarde.* (I remember that afternoon.)
yourTurn.why: With the little *de*, you need *acordarse*: *me acuerdo de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Recuerdo* or *Me acuerdo* and type the whole sentence: *___ su cara.* (I remember his face.)
yourTurn.why: No *de* here, so it is *recordar*: the thing follows directly.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell Don Hernando you remember Rosa.
yourTurn.why: *Me acuerdo de* + a person works; with *recordar* a person takes *a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you remember to pay the electricity bill?
yourTurn.why: Remembering to do something is *acordarse de* + the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't remember his name.
yourTurn.answer: No me acuerdo de su nombre.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I remembered that it was her birthday.
yourTurn.answer: Me acordé de que era su cumpleaños.
yourTurn.why: A whole clause after *acordarse* needs *de que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question for a friend: *Te acuerdas de Rosa.*
yourTurn.why: Same words, now with question marks.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Recordar* takes the thing directly, with no *de*.
*Acordarse* always needs its *de* before the thing you remember.

pitfalls.wrong: Acordé de que era su cumpleaños.
pitfalls.right: Me acordé de que era su cumpleaños.
pitfalls.why: Without *me*, it is a different verb. To remember, you need the *me/te/se*.

personal: Tell Don Hernando one thing you remember well, using *Me acuerdo de…* or *Recuerdo…*.
